provenanceNote: Rebuilt for the 1800 floor. The original used a year inside 0000-0099 as a testing device, pairing a tiny year with a reference date in the same range so that only one branch of CenturyResolver was reachable; the century-00 carve-out is what made constructing it legal. The floor removes that device, and a replacement cannot be constructed because a valid Swedish number with a plausible year is the disclosure risk the corpus rules forbid. Rebuilt instead from Skatteverket's published 190312049802 with a reference date chosen to reach the same branch: the candidate date 1903-12-04 is not after the reference 1903-12-31, so no century is subtracted. Verified to isolate that branch by inverting the comparison in CenturyResolver and watching this fixture fail.

Rebuilt for the 1800 floor; see the sibling fixture for why the original could not simply have its year raised. The mirror branch: the candidate date 2003-12-04 IS after the reference 2003-01-01, so a century is subtracted and the number resolves to 1903 — Skatteverket's published value. Same input as the fixture above, differing only in reference date, which is what makes the pair isolate one branch each.

Twelve digits are century-complete, so this parses without a reference date. It exists to exercise Format::Short with no reference date on the object: rendering it must throw ReferenceDateRequired rather than guess, which the golden dump records as data instead of crashing. `formats` is deliberately omitted here — the conformance harness's formatsMatch test iterates every Format member and would fail on the throw, whereas the golden dump handles it explicitly.

Rebuilt for the 1800 floor, and the most load-bearing of the three. The reference is an instant 30 minutes past midnight in +01:00, whose UTC calendar day is the *previous* day, 2003-12-03. Read in UTC the candidate 2003-12-04 is after the reference, a century is subtracted, and the result is Skatteverket's 190312049802. Read in +01:00 the reference day would be 2003-12-04, the candidate would not be after it, and the number would resolve to 200312049802 — a different person, a century out. This fixture is what pins the decision that reference dates normalise to UTC on entry, recorded in docs/decision-log.md, and it must keep resolving to the 1903 value. The Short rendering is a second, quieter assertion of the same thing: the bearer is 99 at the UTC reference day of 2003-12-03 and so renders '-', where a reference read in +01:00 would put them at 100 on their birthday and render '+'.
